picks.title: Interior with Young Woman Seen from Behind
picks.creator: Vilhelm Hammershøi
picks.licence: Public domain (Wikimedia Commons tag; author died 70+ years ago)
picks.credit: Vilhelm Hammershøi, Interior with Young Woman Seen from Behind, 1903–04, Randers Kunstmuseum. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: A lone woman in black stands with her back to us on the right, facing a bare grey wall; the left half is almost empty wall, an ideal quiet field for the title. Borrow the muted grey palette, the turned-away figure (isolation without melodrama) and the generous negative space.

picks.title: The Monk by the Sea
picks.creator: Caspar David Friedrich
picks.licence: Public domain (Wikimedia Commons tag; author died 70+ years ago)
picks.credit: Caspar David Friedrich, The Monk by the Sea, 1808–10, Alte Nationalgalerie, Berlin. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: One tiny figure against an enormous empty sky and dark sea: the classic image of smallness and solitude. About four-fifths of the canvas is sky, so a title fits in the upper left; the low horizon and desaturated tones carry exhaustion quietly.

picks.title: A Village Choir
picks.creator: Thomas Webster
picks.licence: Public domain (Wikimedia Commons tag; author died 70+ years ago)
picks.credit: Thomas Webster, A Village Choir, 1847, Victoria and Albert Museum, London. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: A crowded church gallery of ordinary villagers singing and playing together, in a warm brown and amber palette. It shows exactly the community-choir-in-a-church idea; borrow the packed, overlapping faces and the warm candle-wood tones for a poster that feels homely, not formal.

picks.title: Watoto Church Choir singing during the 33rd Coronation anniversary
picks.creator: Namwanje Sauyah
picks.licence: CC0 1.0 (as tagged on Commons)
picks.credit: Photo: Namwanje Sauyah, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: A dense row of singers in bright, warm clothing, mouths open mid-song, with faces repeating into the depth of the frame: 'lots of voices together' made visible. It is a church choir but photographed at a civic event, not inside a church, so use it for the crowd rhythm and warmth. Identifiable people: CC0 covers copyright, not personality rights, so check before using it in advertising.

picks.title: Seeing stars (SEST telescope at La Silla)
picks.creator: Sangku Kim / ESO
picks.licence: CC BY 4.0
picks.credit: Sangku Kim/ESO, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: A big dish stands alone under a dark star field, attentive and still. It reads as 'listening and watching' without screens, code or hoodies. Borrow the dark-blue night, the single sensor turned toward the unknown, and the tension of a small lit structure against vast darkness.

picks.title: The IRAM 30-meter telescope scanning the night sky
picks.creator: IRAM-gre (IRAM)
picks.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0
picks.credit: IRAM-gre, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: A radio telescope sweeping the night sky: constant, active vigilance, which is the idea behind security monitoring. Its strong geometric silhouette crops well for a wide hero. Note: CC BY-SA means a modified version (a crop or overlay) must be shared under the same licence, so check that suits the website.

picks.title: Fishermen on beach harvesting salmon catch, vicinity of the lower Columbia River, ca 1900
picks.creator: John Fletcher Ford
picks.date: c. 1900 (University of Washington Libraries, Industries and Occupations Photographs, INDOCC 631)
picks.licence: Public domain (published c. 1900; Commons tag)
picks.credit: John Fletcher Ford, c. 1900. University of Washington Libraries Special Collections. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: A beach covered in salmon from one seine haul shows historic abundance at a glance. Use it as the 'past' half of a then/now contrast, perhaps faded sepia, against a sparse present-day image. The print's 'Copyrighted' caption dates from c. 1900; that copyright has long expired.

picks.title: Sockeye salmon sun glistening
picks.creator: Lisa Hupp / U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service
picks.date: undated (in USFWS 2021 Fish and Aquatic Conservation Annual Report)
picks.licence: Public domain (work of a US federal employee)
picks.credit: Lisa Hupp/USFWS. Public domain.
picks.why: A single red sockeye in clear water: the 'now' half, one fish where there were thousands. Put it small in a lot of empty space, or set it beside the 1900 haul, so the scale gap reads instantly on the cover. Not a US government endorsement; credit USFWS as courtesy.

picks.title: Domaći hljeb sa sjemenkama u pekari (home-style seeded bread in a bakery)
picks.creator: Minja Klarić
picks.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0
picks.credit: Minja Klarić, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: One dark, seed-crusted loaf stands upright in front of a rack of pale white loaves. It is almost exactly the brief: one loaf distinguished by texture and colour. The vertical framing suits a 4:5 or Story crop. CC BY-SA: edits must stay under CC BY-SA, with credit given.

picks.title: The Baker
picks.creator: Job Adriaensz. Berckheyde
picks.licence: Public domain (Wikimedia Commons tag; author died 70+ years ago)
picks.credit: Job Berckheyde, The Baker, c. 1681, Worcester Art Museum. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: A Haarlem baker blows a horn to announce fresh bread, with loaves on the sill: heritage, craft and celebration together. It works as a mood and layout reference for an anniversary post: a window frame, warm light, and the bread presented like a proud announcement.

picks.title: The Avenue at Middelharnis
picks.creator: Meindert Hobbema
picks.licence: Public domain (Wikimedia Commons tag; author died 70+ years ago)
picks.credit: Meindert Hobbema, The Avenue at Middelharnis, 1689, National Gallery, London. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: The textbook one-point perspective: a road lined with tall trees runs straight to a vanishing point on a low horizon, under a big sky. Borrow the converging lines that drag the eye forward, and put 'Where we are going' in the open sky.

picks.title: Historic Route 66 near Amboy, California
picks.creator: Dietmar Rabich
picks.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0
picks.credit: Dietmar Rabich / Wikimedia Commons / CC BY-SA 4.0
picks.why: A straight desert road running to the horizon in a wide panoramic format (about 2:1), so it suits a 16:9 slide. A clean, modern take on the same pull-to-the-horizon idea. CC BY-SA: credit the author; adapted versions must carry the same licence.

picks.title: Moonlight, Wood Island Light
picks.creator: Winslow Homer
picks.licence: Public domain (Wikimedia Commons tag; author died 70+ years ago)
picks.credit: Winslow Homer, Moonlight, Wood Island Light, 1894, The Metropolitan Museum of Art. Public domain.
picks.why: A night sea crashing on rocks, nearly all dark, with a lighthouse's small point of light in the distance. It suits a literary cover: painterly, menacing, restrained. Borrow the near-black palette and the single distant light as the focal point.

picks.title: Sidi Bou Afi Lighthouse, El Jadida, Morocco
picks.creator: Belbachirkamal
picks.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0
picks.credit: Belbachirkamal, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: A lighthouse at night in fog, its beams visible as solid shafts against a dark sky, in portrait orientation like a book cover. Borrow the beam as a graphic element, which can also point to the title. CC BY-SA: the cover design built on it may need to be licensed CC BY-SA, so a commercial publisher may prefer it as a reference only.

picks.title: Nocturne: Blue and Silver – Chelsea
picks.creator: James McNeill Whistler
picks.licence: Public domain (Wikimedia Commons tag; author died 70+ years ago)
picks.credit: James McNeill Whistler, Nocturne: Blue and Silver – Chelsea, 1871, Tate. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: Almost a single field of soft blue-green with a low horizon, a few faint lights and one small boat. It is the calmest image I know, and easy to crop wide. Borrow the one-hue palette, the misty edges and the near-absence of detail for a sleep banner with text overlaid.

picks.title: Moonlight, Strandgade 30
picks.creator: Vilhelm Hammershøi
picks.licence: CC0 (The Met Open Access; public-domain painting)
picks.credit: Vilhelm Hammershøi, Moonlight, Strandgade 30, 1900–06, The Metropolitan Museum of Art (Open Access, CC0).
picks.why: An empty room at night, with soft moonlight from a window falling on the wall and floor. It feels hushed and domestic, like a bedroom just before sleep. Borrow the low-contrast greys, the single soft light source, and the absence of anything busy.

picks.title: Meeting of Waters (Manaus)
picks.creator: Ana Claudia Jatahy – MTUR (Brazilian Ministry of Tourism)
picks.licence: CC0 (as tagged on Commons, from the Ministry of Tourism Flickr)
picks.credit: Ana Claudia Jatahy / MTUR, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: The dark Rio Negro and the sandy Solimões run side by side as one river without mixing at first: two departments that are clearly different but now share one channel. Borrow the clean two-tone split for the slide, with each half labelled.

picks.title: Confluence de l'Arve et du Rhône (Geneva)
picks.creator: Christian David
picks.licence: CC BY 4.0
picks.credit: Christian David, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: The clear blue Rhône meets the silty grey Arve and they flow on together, with a visible seam between them. It is a European, urban counterpart to the Manaus image, and the high-resolution landscape format suits a slide. Credit the author.

picks.title: Rain, Steam and Speed – The Great Western Railway
picks.creator: J. M. W. Turner
picks.licence: Public domain (Wikimedia Commons tag; author died 70+ years ago)
picks.credit: J. M. W. Turner, Rain, Steam and Speed – The Great Western Railway, 1844, National Gallery, London. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: A locomotive bursts out of golden haze along a diagonal bridge: the classic painting of energy and the new rushing forward. Borrow the strong diagonal, the warm, high-energy palette and the motion blur for a spread about growth, while keeping the reference abstract rather than literally Victorian.

picks.title: Night Light Trail, Maryland, Lagos, Nigeria
picks.creator: Omoeko Media
picks.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0
picks.credit: Omoeko Media, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: A long exposure of traffic streaming through Lagos at night: literal forward motion in a fast-growing emerging-market city, which avoids generic stock skylines. Borrow the streaking light lines as a directional graphic motif across the spread. CC BY-SA: adaptations must stay under the same licence; I did not view this image myself.
